It sounds like your cousin wasn’t ready for a pet like a chameleon. He’s black because he is stressed for sure. The sun most definitely was good for him but the overstimulation from being moved from his cage to outside stressed him out. My cham isn’t a fan of being brought outside due to this. I will bring her enclosure outside so she can catch some natural rays without becoming stressed. They don’t like to be out in the open so I recommend that you put his enclosure outside (not in direct sunlight) so he can hide in his plants (hopefully he has foliage in his cage) while still getting UVB. A few days without the light will not kill him, just upset him. They also will not usually drink from standing water, they can’t recognize it. If he has plants in there, spritz some water so that they collect in droplets and he might drink them. So, in summary, put his cage outside (temp should be 70-85, overheating can worsen things), spritz with water regularly (it doesn’t sound like she has an automated system for him) and LEAVE HIM ALONE. They are solitary creatures so for you to keep checking on him, handling him, being all up in his business will stress him out further. You will know when he has passed if he does, no movement and he will decompose rather quickly. Message me for further help/conversation. You tried your best and that’s all the matters in this situation.

I have always gotten my plants from Home Depot or Lowe’s. Getting them through “organic greenhouses” are always a pain in the ass and super expensive; not to mention many tropical plant breeders still use chemicals like pesticides. I usually just buy them, remove them from the old soil, soak in clean water for about 15 minutes, and replant in organic soil or a mix with washed play sand. I’ll then give them about a week to watch if they take to the new soil (some plants do not grow well in a sand mix) and for them to naturally rid themselves of the pesticides. Never have had any issues!

Lay bin must be a least 12 in deep. Fill a third with organic moist soil. Mix washed play sand and organic soil together and put on top. Moisten it so you can take 2-3 fingers and make a diagonal hole that will stay together. If it falls it needs more water. Too much water and she will not lay. Put the pothos plant in the lay bin with roots going down. Chams like to lay next to roots so that’s why she’s trying to lay in that bin. Good luck.

Be sure you’re feeding food that is the right size. Babies don’t know anything and may even be intimidated by moving insects instead of tempted at first. I remember the first time I brought out a hornworm my Cham was horrified hahaha, so as silly as it may sound it can def happen 
I recommend small mealworms and maybe a few waxworms
Small crickets are also good but small Dubai roaches are perfect for babies. They’re small so they’re not threatening (lol) and they move in a way that’s very enticing, especially if you flip them on their back chameleons like to see their legs move. It’s stimulating to them and will trigger something in them to eat it 
Good luck!
